identity.objective: Test whether Flow requires primitive status or is faithfully representable as a first-class derived dynamical object over the ten RGR-02 headings.

evidence_refs: Encyclopedia of Mathematics: Flow (continuous-time dynamical system)
Baez & Pollard: A Compositional Framework for Reaction Networks
Fong & Spivak: An Invitation to Applied Category Theory
assumptions: M0 and M1 receive equal conceptual standing at challenge entry.
No human/clinical/Elemental data is required to decide formal reducibility.
Architectural usefulness does not imply primitive status.
unknowns: Whether any candidate Flow property resists representation by the ten-heading scaffold.
Whether future empirical 05B evidence will show advantages for an explicit derived Flow object.

acceptance_conditions: Attempt genuine M0 reduction across all candidate Flow fields.
Use independent formal sources from multiple mathematical traditions.
Do not use Burger, CSF spiritual interpretation, or Elemental Alchemy to decide primitive status.
Return NOT EARNED if Flow is representable without hidden variables.
Keep runtime and member-facing authority closed.
falsification_conditions: A candidate Flow field is declared irreducible without showing why existing RGR roles cannot express it.
The result confuses centrality with formal primitiveness.
The result relies on Elemental labels or metaphysical claims.
A runtime implementation is smuggled into the formal challenge.
stop_conditions: Formal source grounding cannot distinguish definition from analogy.

guard.authorized_core_snapshot: Formal reducibility challenge only; Flow primitive status may be rejected; no runtime/member authority.
